summary.name: Software testing
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article explaining software testing: the practice of checking whether software meets its intended objectives, covering its goals, categories, levels, and techniques.
use_cases: learning the types of software testing
understanding the test pyramid for automated testing
choosing between black-box and white-box approaches
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software tool. It defines software testing as checking whether software meets its intended objectives, and distinguishes dynamic testing (running code) from static testing (reviewing code and documentation). It describes testing levels (unit, integration, system/end-to-end), black-box, white-box and grey-box approaches, and specialised types such as regression, smoke, acceptance, alpha and beta testing. It also covers code coverage metrics (function, statement, decision coverage) and test automation as part of CI/CD.
notable: Explains the test pyramid of unit, integration and end-to-end tests
Covers black-box, white-box and grey-box testing approaches
Lists code coverage metrics: function, statement and decision coverage
caveats: Encyclopedia article, not a software product; it does not provide tools to download
Page notes its style may not be encyclopedic and some sections contain excessive detail
States that testing can show correctness only for specific scenarios and cannot find all bugs
